pr_body:
Note this relies on PR : https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/45827

- Add support for CloseOutputAsync
- Remove `[ActiveIssue("https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/45468", TestPlatforms.Browser)]`
- Add more tests

Fix https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/46909
Fix https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/45468
Fix https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/45674
Fix https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/45586
Close https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/46983

Comments from parent PR:

Multiple fixes for Abort.

There are multiple failures with the Abort tests causing some tests to:

- Never end
- Multiple GC calls that end in running out of memory. 

- Some failures are expected to fail with specific WebSocketError codes:

Error codes that are not correct tend to be when websockets tests are looking for specific error codes and messages when the browser returns `NativeError` and the websocket native error code instead.

```
failed: WebSocket is closed before the connection is established.
```

---

These need to be marked correctly and or caught and wrapped correctly.

```
Assert.Equal() Failure
  info: Expected: Aborted
  info: Actual:   Closed
```

Fixes for these should also fix some, note not all, of the memory runtime errors as per issue: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/45586

--- 

Fix tests that were failing when expecting CloseSent as a valid state.  

```
// fail: [FAIL] System.Net.WebSockets.Client.Tests(server: ws://corefx-net-http11.azurewebsites.net/WebSocket/EchoWebSocket.ashx)
//   info: Assert.Throws() Failure
//   info: Expected: typeof(System.OperationCanceledException)
//   info: Actual:   typeof(System.Net.WebSockets.WebSocketException): The WebSocket is in an invalid state ('Aborted') for this operation. Valid states are: 'Open, CloseSent'
```

---

Tests are intermittently failing with System.OperationCanceledException : The operation was canceled.

~~Added ActiveIssue for these two tests.  https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/46909~~

```
It seems that sometimes the default timeout is not enough for browser so it is extended for browser environments
See issue https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/46909
```

Further addressed in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/47906


---

SendReceive_PartialMessageBeforeCompleteMessageArrives_Success which describes the test as Ask the remote server to echo back received messages without ever signaling "end of message".  This test hangs as javascript fetch does not support this functionality.

See issue https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/46983 for more detailed description and native javascript tests.

---

Associate PR's: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/44666 and https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/45470

Close https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/45586
Fix https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/45674

issue_context.title: [browser][websockets] CloseOutputAsync is not supported
issue_context.body:
Right now this is not supported on browser and tests are failing.

Added this issue as a placeholder to deactivate theses tests.

JavaScript WebSocket does not support a `CloseOutputAsync` but one may be able fake it so these tests work or maybe we keep the not supported instead of faking something that really is not used.

part of: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/44666

@BrennanConroy 

Moved your [comments from the other PR](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/45536#discussion_r537723055) to here to be tracked:

> Unrelated to this PR. Are there plans to implement this method? If not, can it be marked as unsupported in the browser? (I'd really like it if this was implemented as per below)
> 
> I know the browser doesn't provide an API for partial closes like this, but it would be very useful to fake it by clearing the websockets handlers and calling `onclose` inline.
> 
> You can see what we did in SignalR to not have possible long delays between calling `close` and the `onclose` callback being invoked.
> https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/0ace31c91138d258008f9547478d156a97f1a87e/src/SignalR/clients/ts/signalr/src/WebSocketTransport.ts#L144-L146
> https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/0ace31c91138d258008f9547478d156a97f1a87e/src/SignalR/clients/ts/signalr/src/WebSocketTransport.ts#L156-L170

review_comments: I'd just like to reiterate that not calling `onClose` manually here could result in a large delay. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/45468#issuecomment-741519725

@BrennanConroy I saw that but is there anyway we can test this easily?

Here is the sequence of event on CloseOutputAsync that is proposed.

- Remove all event delegates not just on the close event or is close event enough?
- Call JavaScript `close()` method on `websocket`.
- Call JavaScript `onClose` event manually on the `websocket`.

I ask because if I leave the code as is the `onClose` will be called as well but the dotnet method returns immediately.

We clear all events on the `websocket` (including `onClose`), call `websocket.close()` then call the user provided `onClose` method manually.

If you can write a test that blocks in `websocket.close()` and checks that the `onClose` method is still called then that would be good.

Have to admit not sure how that would be done from the test harness for Websocket Client.  

Will add the code above.  Thanks for the feedback.
